themes.consensus_view: Banks broadly flag the Strait of Hormuz situation as a live oil-supply risk, but they split on duration: Rabobank expects the blockade to drag through September while SEB and MUFG position for a reopening that would normalize prices and reignite demand.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple desks treat the Strait of Hormuz situation as an active supply-chain and energy-supply risk shaping their macro outlook.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz closure impacting global energy supply
Strait of Hormuz supply chain disruption
Strait of Hormuz energy supply disruption

facts_contested.claim: Duration of the Hormuz blockade / timing of reopening
facts_contested.for_evidence: we now assume that Hormuz is likely to be out of normal action up to September
facts_contested.against_evidence: Expect to see a resurgence in demand to rebuild stocks and reserves

themes.consensus_view: Banks broadly agree the AI buildout is still accelerating, with hyperscaler spending, cloud backlogs and supply constraints all pointing higher, while Deutsche Bank flags that this capex boom is helping push inflation up rather than down.

facts_agreed.claim: Demand for AI compute and data center capacity is outrunning supply, supporting continued buildout.
evidence_quotes: This combination of rising monetization, backlog growth, and constrained supply helps explain why the AI buildout still has room to run.
Today we are still severely compute constrained and Jevons Paradox remains the axiomatic ruler
Demand from data centers is outpacing supply across the board.

facts_agreed.claim: Hyperscalers and big tech are pouring record capital into AI infrastructure.
evidence_quotes: AI exuberance remains a key theme, however, with the announcement of an $80 billion fundraising
signals a strategic pivot from providing compute capacity... to providing the seamless, production-ready infrastructure

facts_agreed.claim: AI infrastructure beneficiaries are seeing strong earnings momentum and equity repricing.
evidence_quotes: stellar quarter that put it on track to hit long-term financial targets
raise our target multiple to reflect increased confidence in CSCO’s positioning to benefit

facts_contested.claim: Whether the AI capex boom is disinflationary or inflationary
facts_contested.for_evidence: Contrary to popular belief, there are no signs that AI is disinflationary
facts_contested.against_evidence: This combination of rising monetization, backlog growth, and constrained supply helps explain why the AI buildout still has room to run.

themes.consensus_view: Banks broadly expect the European Central Bank to raise interest rates at its June meeting, with no desk arguing against the move.

facts_agreed.claim: The ECB is poised to deliver a rate hike at its June meeting.
evidence_quotes: We expect a pre-emptive (insurance) hike of 25bps in the deposit rate
Wunsch in an interview with the Financial Times joined Schnabel in clearly signalling a rate hike

themes.consensus_view: Seven banks flag US-Iran tensions and negotiations as a live geopolitical backdrop, but none has staked a directional view on how it resolves or what to trade against it.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks reference US-Iran tensions and negotiations as an ongoing geopolitical backdrop without taking a directional stance.
evidence_quotes: US-Iran clashes in the Middle East

themes.consensus_view: Banks see the US job market softening but not breaking, with mixed signals between still-elevated job openings and a forecast slowdown in May hiring.

facts_agreed.claim: Banks expect May US payrolls to come in softer than April but not alarmingly weak.
evidence_quotes: We expect softer jobs data for May as compared to April, but nothing too concerning.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks describe the US labor market as cooling, stabilizing, resilient, or in a low-hiring/low-firing regime rather than collapsing.
evidence_quotes: US labor market low hiring-low firing regime

facts_contested.claim: Whether US labor demand is firming or cooling
facts_contested.for_evidence: V/U jumped above 1.0 for the first time since Jun ’25

themes.consensus_view: Four banks flag component supply chain constraints across semiconductors, diodes, lasers and data center hardware as a live issue, but none has staked a directional trading view on it.

facts_agreed.claim: Banks across multiple desks reference component supply chain constraints spanning semiconductors, diodes, lasers and data center hardware as a live backdrop.
evidence_quotes: Supply shortages in semiconductors and electrical components

themes.consensus_view: Banks see AI resilience as the new key driver of stock performance in info services, with execution mattering more than broad AI fear, though some flag AI-driven security threats as a risk.

facts_agreed.claim: AI risk is no longer the dominant driver of returns in info services; execution and structural AI resilience differentiate winners.
evidence_quotes: AI risk is no longer the primary driver of returns and relative performance increasingly reflects execution
agencies are most resilient to technological change in their data and healthcare businesses

facts_agreed.claim: Banks across multiple desks reference AI as a live driver of productivity, optimism, and security risk.
